cases.description: One normalized design element is instantiated by one approved method step with exact source lineage.
Method predecessor step is translated into a same-element task dependency edge.
One approved method template is instantiated for multiple unique design elements.
Permuting element and step input vectors yields identical graph and topological order.
A required source property is absent; compiler must not invent a default.
An element task family is outside the approved template applicability.
Identical source and target units preserve the source value and source reference.
A unit mismatch without external conversion evidence is rejected.
Explicit externally approved conversion binds converted value and evidence reference.
Duplicate physical design element identity cannot generate duplicate tasks.
Duplicate method step identifiers are rejected.
A step dependency referencing no template step is rejected.
A cyclic method template cannot compile into a work graph.
Ambiguous property names are rejected; first-match selection is prohibited.
Two method mappings cannot silently overwrite the same target parameter.
Every mapped property requires an explicit source reference.
Unapproved or unreferenced method template cannot compile.
Empty design manifests or method templates cannot compile to empty success.
Length-prefixed task identities distinguish identifiers containing separators.
Compiler preserves the method's declared capability obligation without claiming it is satisfied.
Independent evidence obligations are copied from the approved method step.
Multiple method dependencies are preserved as distinct task edges.
Target frame is mandatory and not inferred.
A changed site epoch must alter the compiled graph identity.
Incomplete conversion evidence cannot produce a parameter value.
Changing the target coordinate frame changes the graph identity even when model/method/template inputs are otherwise identical.
